t:
You are now in Eden. It's All-Mother's divine garden she created for her beloved daughter. And the ideal hideout from the Darkness. Eden is a secret world. Nihaz has no idea where it is. The void between the worlds is endless. The number of worlds evolving around their Suns is endless. Even if Nihaz has all the time in the world, he won't be able to find All-Mother.

Nihaz's followers have been looking for All-Mother for millions of years. Every time she managed to escape.

Eden has a perfect symbiosis of plants and animals. They all exist together, and they can't do without one another. Eden's greatest mystery is the Great Tree. The embodiment of All-Mother's divine powers. The amazing plants give birth to the forces of Creation and Life.

The smallest Tree sprout can take root in the void and create matter around it.

All-Mother's great plan is to plant the Tree sprouts in all worlds, thus bringing the life in all corners of the Universe.
r154384.n: I want to ask about Eden, the world of Life

t:
Eidos is the primal world, which stores samples of everything that exists and ideas that could be incarnated in future worlds. This is the root cause why many things are very much alike in different worlds, even if their creators might add their personal touch.

Sadly, Nihaz chose Eidos as his primary target during the Great War. Thanks to the betrayal of one of All-Mother's daughters, he passed the ingenious defenses, put up by other gods, and sneaked into this world.

Eidos was conquered by the Darkness. Its secrets now belonged to the Dark God. It became the battlefield in the upcoming wars between Nihaz's followers and the worlds of Inis and Enod.

Finally, the battles of gods destroyed Eidos to the ground. Some of the things that had once belonged to Eidos were saved. They are now here, on Eden, waiting for All-Mother to begin a new cycle. Others were taken by Nihaz, giving him dangerous benefits in many regards.

Lucky for us, Nihaz cannot create Life. All he is capable of is corrupting and distorting other gods' creations. The knowledge of Eidos has made him a master of shifting and shaping the matter.
r154385.n: I want to ask about Eidos, the primal world

t:
Anrok is one of the worlds where the Light fights against the Darkness. It has a rich history. Initially inhabited by refugees of other worlds, eventually it began its own way of development. Powerful mages and brave warriors fought one another to rule the world. Many were tempted by the Darkness, others rejected temptations. Do I need to tell you all stories of the world?

About brothers who fought to death for the throne? About the daughter who took back her father's kingdom by force? There are so many stories...
r154387.n: I want to ask about Anrok

t:
Ardan is the world where gods participate in everything. The laws of All-Mother are same in all worlds. Some smaller domains are often divided by forces, same as the inner worlds. These smaller forces make weird alliances, which might differ from those here. But the darkness is always darkness. Thankfully, Nihaz isn't omnipresent or omniscient. His dark minions act by the laws we know, even though their lord wants to break the Great Circle.

Ardan is the world where his effort doesn't bear fruit. It still lives the rightful life.

The darkness is eternal but mortals can fight it.
r154388.n: I want to ask about Ardan

t:
Ascolet is another world where the confrontation of two forces predetermine the existence. At fate would have it, these forces are exact opposite. Just think. There are two alliances. One belongs to the mages that resemble your Great Mages. The other belongs to proud kings, who put the ban on any witchery whatsoever. It is also made impossible by a mysterious artifact at the border between the enemies.

Moreover, each alliance is supported by mysterious forces of Order and Chaos, and their feud has lasted much longer than the feud between knights and sorcerers.
r154389.n: I want to ask about Ascolet

t:
Atla is faithful to All-Mother, although the mortals there have no idea of her existence. Each of the outer worlds is unique, and they all have something in common. Such races as elves or humans aren't uncommon in other worlds. Creators tend to repeat and reproduce their best creations. The prototypes of all living things were stored in Eidos.

I think even in your world, the races have fought wars to rule your world. This is what happened in Atla. The elves were banished from their lands by a young race of people. They tried to reclaim what was lost. This led to the conflict that involved all people of Atla. This war was a battleground for the living as well as for the divine powers. The Light fought against the Darkness. The Chaos tried to destroy the Order.
r154390.n: I want to ask about Atla

t:
This world of red ocean and white sand, dotted with pillars of stone, is under attack by monsters from worlds ruled by chaos. However, there is hope - the inhabitants of the world have found a way to fight back. I heard you use ingenious technical devices in Sarnaut - they are like a second set of clothes for you. The inhabitants of Ayanami have gone much further - their suits are huge structures created to fight against the giants of the world of Chaos. It's surprisingly effective, though I don't think mortals' addiction to these tricks will do them any good.

But now the hope of that world rests only on those who know how to manage such mechanisms. It is a pity that this world does not have its own protector gods, and they can only hope that the devices they have created will be stronger than monsters.
r154391.n: I want to talk about Ayanami

t:
Darien was one of the outer worlds, where Nihaz's promises gave bitter fruit. Like many others, this world was divided by hostile elements.
 The rivalry between the four siblings, each representing their own element, resulted in the emergence of the fifth element. It became the base for the new order, the heartless technology, hostile towards everyone and everything.
 Later this war extended to nearby worlds and became the arena of a great rivalry, which was no longer about victory. Both parties wanted complete destruction of one another.
r154392.n: I want to ask about Darien

t:
It is usually the responsibility of the gods to protect their worlds, but in this world, things turned out differently - a treaty was made that placed this duty on the shoulders of mortals. A limited confrontation is preferable to a large-scale war with unknown consequences - both the defenders and the conquerors decided so.

The result was a tournament. The world whose representatives win this tournament is declared the winner and can decide the fate of the defeated. I believe it to be reasonable, because that's how the fate of the worlds is decided by heroes and the gods these heroes serve. Everything is in accord with the precepts of the All-Mother.

Unfortunately, not everything is as good on Ditsu Vango. Having failed to defeat the defenders of this world in a fair fight, the conquerors resorted to numerous tricks, trying to circumvent the rules of the tournament. So far, their intrigues have ended in failure, but who knows what will happen in the future?
r154393.n: I want to know about Ditsu Vango

t:
This world is full of magic. Despite that, the inhabitants of Dunkel have very advanced technology. Perhaps it's because magic is perceived by them as something unnatural, otherworldly. This world is indeed a little darker than usual. In addition to humans, it is inhabited by a large number of small races that live their own lives and do not claim supremacy. They hide behind the walls of houses where humans live, inhabit dense forests where humans do not set foot.

But sometimes their paths cross. "Miracles" take place then. Humans are always amazed whenever they meet a part of their world they normally ignore. In addition to the minor races, Dunkel is full of undead that are more friendly than hostile, and also talking animals - individuals that are sentient for some strange reason.
r154394.n: I want to talk about Dunkel

t:
Eshan. I have a lot to say about it. The struggle of the opposing forces, the Order and Chaos, the Light and Darkness, is taking place there. History of this world has been dark. Nihaz couldn't lead its people astray like in Anrok. It was affected by the Chaos much more than by the Darkness.

I heard that Sarn was imprisoned in the heart of your world. The same way as the powerful god of Chaos was imprisoned here. He did everything in his power to break free. Just like Sarn.

Unfortunately for this world's people, there was a breach in his prison. Creation of Chaos used it to enter the mortal worlds.

They reached the highest success after one of the queens got under the influence of a mighty general of the Chaos armies and helped them carry out their plans.
r154395.n: I want to ask about Eshan

t:
Another world that doesn't have a lot of magic. It's frozen on the edge between what you call "technological progress" and the old ways conforming to the All-Mother's precepts. Yes, Fabella is one step away from taking the path that Nihaz led his worlds to, and so far no one can say in which direction the unstable balance will shift.

The difference between Fabella and many worlds is that the race inhabiting it is divided into many peoples, and each of them has created their own civilization. Now in this world, wars for supremacy are raging. Swords cross, bows sing, all to determine who will prevail.

Each of these peoples considers themselves the most worthy. They all have their own advantages and disadvantages. Who will win? Who will lose? It's not clear yet.
r154396.n: I want to talk about Fabella

t: What kind of world is this? The border of savagery and civilization where dust, gold, and weapons form the basis of life. Harsh conditions breed harsh morals, and here being true to one's word isn't worth much, so in fights beloved by the inhabitants of this world, the winner is usually the one that plays dirty. However, there is beauty here, too - spaces untouched by humans, wild animals that are not pushed out by the cars you love so much. It is a pity that none of this is valued as much as gold. This is truly cursed metal, but for some reason it's loved the most by the inhabitants of this world.
r154397.n: I want to ask about Garnecott

t:
Another world of technology. However, on Girheim, it took on a very bizarre look. Due to the fact that this world is poor in natural resources, its inhabitants are forced to make do with what they have. Yes, they build their machines, but those machines are based on different principles compared to whatever is used in other technological worlds.

Perhaps this is precisely the reason the technology of this world is more like magic than the technology in other worlds. Based on what I've seen, I can say that it's similar to your manatech, only instead of magic it works on the power of heated water.

Indeed, in any world, mortals will find any way to achieve what they want!

The inhabitants of this world also build airships, only they rise into the air with the help of special balls filled with gases that are lighter than air.
r154398.n: I want to talk about Girheim

t:
Cyros is one of the outer worlds, possessed by Darkness. This world remembers and respects the will of All-Mother. Its dwellers are attacked by sinister creatures beneath the surface. It's riddled with tunnels and caves, opening on the surface. Defenders of this world are fighting against the dungeon kings... not very successfully.

A new war began when one of these Guardians began an aggressive campaign against the human Empire protected by the power of one of the light goddesses. He managed to achieve a lot and defeated the other dungeon masters, but in the end, he himself became a victim of betrayal.
r154399.n: I want to ask about Cyros

t:
I know that your world was broken up by the Great Mages, craving for power. They dealt irreparable damage in their pursuit of power. Sarnaut is not the only world where this has happened. Carpey was also destroyed after the mages instigated a war over leadership.
 Each of them wanted to take the world's power, but in the end, one of them cast a destructive spell that was supposed to stop the others. Instead, the spell broke the world. Its shards were filled with monsters that attacked the greedy mages.
r154400.n: I want to ask about Carpey

t:
Are there any worlds completely possessed by the Darkness? Yes, there are. Crippla is one of them. This world is old enough, and it's gone way beyond All-Mother's plan. It's not the only problem. Evil is done openly in Crippla. Dark cults worshipping the dark gods seized power, and the ancient monsters awakened. One by one, the cities fell under their control. Bloody sacrifices began.

The God of Death has supreme power here, which might have been the reason for all of the above. He forgot his duty, and he simply loves torturing mortals. His power over the souls of the dead allows him to raise the undead who hate the guts of the living.

Those who saw the doomed world understand what we are dealing with.

The last data I received mentions a certain avenger. He was one of the members of the cult organized by this sinister god but, like his friends, he was betrayed and killed. He rose from the dead, thirsting for revenge, and succeeded - the deity of death, which neglected his duties, was destroyed.
r154401.n: I want to ask about Crippla

t:
Lafia might seem a happy little world.

It might be true. At first sight. Its people don't suffer from wars or disasters. This is a happy place, although there are the poor and unhappy here, as well.

There's another problem. The souls of people here have long been consumed by Nihaz's darkness. All they want is pleasure and joy. Their world is full of fun devices designed for pleasure.

The price for it is emptiness inside. They don't want anything in life but to gain more, take more, consume more.

Your world could have gone the same way. Several safe centuries, and you all end up like Lafia!

For some reason, the messenger sent to this world became extremely interested in one of the completely unremarkable mortals who was considered a failure even among their fellow tribesmen. The Herald discovered that it was this mortal's Thread of Destiny that was intimately intertwined with the fate of the world. The tapestry woven by fate is bizarre, if it is true.
r154402.n: I want to ask about Lafia

t:
I hear there are vampires in Sarnaut. They aren't unique to your world. They sucked out dry almost all people of Lacona.

I suppose, the root cause of vampirism lies in Ossu. Another All-Mother's world is a haven for many dark creatures of the ancient eons. Vampires are perfect spreaders of the Darkness. They can hide out for a long time, and then come out and infect everyone around them.

That's what happened in Lacona. According to my sources, one of the most powerful vampires awoke there. Whether he belonged to another world or was born on Lacona, I do not know.

But he infected most of the people before they hunted him down.

Alas, some of the vampires escaped. Several centuries later, a much more powerful burst of vampirism broke out on Lacona and swallowed the entire world.
r154403.n: I want to ask about Lacona

t:
Marn is an outer world, where two forces are fighting. It's hard to name these forces, though. It's a complex mixture of Darkness, Chaos, and elemental magic. I hear, there was once a Leper in Sarnaut that corrupted the living, turning them into monsters.

We have something similar here. It's called Blight. The curious effect is that any magic triggers the Blight to spread. As a consequence, all magic is banned by the authorities of the world. There's an Order that hunts down all kinds of sorcerers and mages.

They prefer to solve their issues with steel weapons. Even a trace of the Blight can't make it inside this world.
r154404.n: I want to ask about Marn

t:
Almid is one of the most technologically advanced worlds. I'm not surprised. There's no magic that could make its dwellers' lives easier. There's no magic in this world whatsoever!

Many people and many countries are allied there. They always create new weapons and armored machinery, deadlier and complex.

Fortunately, they haven't yet destroyed their own world, but it isn't due to them being particularly reasonable. Outsiders interfered at some point.

A while ago they stole a crystal of ambrosia left at the battlefield where All-Mother and Nihaz's army fought. Outsiders cracked some of its properties and managed to grow more crystals, even though this form of divine life energy is only a reflection of its true self. So they spread ambrosia across other worlds, because all worlds can give their own Life power.

One of the crystals ended up on Almid. Due to the magic power, it began to grow. Just like you, people discovered its properties and started a hunt. It was the reason for more conflicts. The war has been on for a whole century!
r154405.n: I want to ask about Almid

t:
Oztra. One of the worlds that has faced some tragic effects of advancement of science and technology. Even though Oztra was a world without magic, they created something truly devastating.

People, whose souls were affected by Nihaz's darkness, made a horrible discovery. In attempts to get a handle on stubborn neighbors, they found a way to split the smallest particle, the basis of everything in the Universe. This is how a weapon of unprecedented power was invented. As it turned out, splitting of the particle released a massive wave of energy.

They found a way to use it peacefully, of course... but its main application was to create weapons. Two empires, who, to be honest, didn't have so many issues, just kept arming themselves, striving to win the race. None of the sides survived to enjoy the victory.

The war started by mistake. The only consequence was destruction. The world of Oztra was incinerated by the advanced weapon. Its cities burned in blinding sheets of white flames. The survivors had to adjust to the new reality.

The luckiest ones managed to find refuge in bomb shelters. Others had to survive on the devastated surface. And then everything has fallen silent... until the new war, where people fought for the remaining resources.

Oztra will never change. Let its fate teach a good lesson to others.
r154406.n: I want to ask about Oztra

t:
I have seen many alien worlds through the Tree, but few have surprised me. Ptolia is one of the worlds that managed to do that.

The amazing thirst for knowledge of the inhabitants of this world led to the fact that they began to collect it and store it. Perhaps the creator god of that world was the root cause, or maybe one of the mortals decided that this was worth doing, but in the end, this whole world became a giant library.

Here on Eden, we certainly think that our Trees are a much better way to gather information, but the Trees store images rather than words, so perhaps there is some sense in these actions. Perhaps, here is no such knowledge that would Ptolia does not possess - after all, the magically enchanted library is endless. Few people understand how new books appear there - perhaps the world itself absorbs the knowledge of our universe and turns it into written works...

I also know that Hirkalla and the Wanderer were in Ptolia and learned a lot there. This makes me think that perhaps such availability of knowledge is not always a good thing.
r154407.n: I want to talk about Ptolia

t:
Nihaz covered your world under the twelve seals, and it was fascinating. While searching for similar cases in the Great Tree's memories, I came across a curious story. The world of Rhun was full of refugees from another world, driven away from their homeland by Nihaz's Darkness. After a while, they realized that his dark servants were following them. Fearing another invasion, they came up with the idea of their own Seals of Protection.

It is obvious that mortals aren't gods but their talents and skills were so good that they could seal twelve divine powers in twelve simple everyday objects.

And thus, the whole world was sealed. They isolated Rhun from the Darkness but as a consequence they were cut off the world magic. Alas! The objects, that were now seals, turned out to be quite fragile. Generations later, people forgot the very art of sealing the divine powers.

Mortals have short memories. Even though the creators made sure that the objects became hallowed relics, centuries later some of the Seals were broken in a fit of arrogance. It was much easier than in your world, but then again, the consequences weren't as grave. Little by little, the Darkness leaked into the world of Rhun. Its adherents insisted that the remaining Seals should be broken too. Sounds familiar, doesn't it?

I wish the memories weren't so sketchy. I have no idea how the story ended. Did the mortals defend their world? Did they fall in an uneven fight with the Darkness?
r154408.n: I want to ask about Rhun

t:
Any of the world histories is just a reflection of the Great War. Mortals may be unaware of Nihaz and Sarn, of All-Mother's great duty of looking after the Universal cycle of life... they may have their own beliefs, their own deities and demons. But then everything that has ever existed is just a part of the Great Circle. The powers of domains reflect in the fates of lesser deities.

Mortals often fall under the impression that Darkness, Chaos, and Death are evil in themselves. It's wrong. They're natural parts of the cycle. Darkness isn't evil per se. The evil was born when Nihaz decided to turn against All-Mother's will and transform everything that existed as he wanted.

Truth be told, when I hear about the deeds of lesser gods, I understand how mortals see evil in them.

The world of Sanctuar was the arena for massacre and bloodbath, for confrontation of all kids of gods. Most of them were the embodiment of evil and disgust, but their rivals, claiming to be warriors of Light and Warriors, were hardly any different.

Sarn in his eclipse of reason created monsters, similar to Chaos beasts from the outer worlds. They are known as demons to people of Sarnaut, whereas the true demons are the lesser gods of Sanctuar, deadly and savage, always at war. They are the ones responsible for a large part of Sanctuar's troubles.
r154409.n: I want to ask about Sanctuar

t:
A wise man told me about Tep, and his ideas and plans on Irdrich that he learned from someone. It's amazing, actually. The insane mage touched the mind of one of the Architect's shards, embraced his idea of the Absolute Order, and decided to carry it out on his own.

Something seems weird, tough. Tep has constructed an ideal virtual illusion for you, hasn't he? I wonder why he went with this particular paradise island with a struggle between Aviak tribes as a natural part of it. Has he considered it an ideal trap for all of you?

Perhaps, such interpretation of his ideas reveals the mystery of his sick mind. According to the Great Tree's memories, he isn't unique in this regard. The idea of settling everyone down in a virtual illusion of sorts isn't all that original. Some used magic for it, others developed sophisticated devices for that purpose.

This is what happened in the world of Synth, where a certain organization gained power. It connected all dwellers of this world to its own network of illusions via control implants in their heads. The much brighter and richer illusory world had nothing to with the dull and gray reality.

Similar to what happened on Irdrich, there were people that managed to escape from the virtual reality and start a resistance movement. Two powers clashed in a battle for minds and souls of this world's dwellers. I know not who won... but the very thought that it was once possible is scary.
r154410.n: I want to ask about Synth

t:
Stargar is just one of the worlds we'll talk about if we remember it exists. The thing is, its inhabitants have long settled on many other worlds that surrounded Stargar, and now this world is only the center of their vast kingdom. Yes, the All-Mother seeks to prevent this, but to our surprise, the inhabitants of this world turned out to be very resistant to Nihaz's influence. And while their hope for the created mechanisms was great, they did not forget their roots.

However, in this story there was a moment when the darkness was stronger. Once upon a time, order in this star kingdom was provided by an order of knights, but there was a traitor in their ranks. He killed the king and almost ended the dynasty, and only a few of the knights were able to escape. The kingdom fell.

Since then, the influence of Darkness has only grown. The state that replaced the kingdom turned out to be unable to maintain the previous order, but in the darkest hour, a true heir was found and returned to power. Stargar became the way it was before. Who knows, maybe this world will be one of those that will help us defeat the Darkness?
r154411.n: I want to talk about Stargar

t:
When I first saw you in our world, found out your names and the differences between you, I couldn't help but remember this world.

It is pretty unique, though I've heard of others like it. Perhaps one of the gods who previously served Sarn is creating worlds based on a motif they discovered somewhere.

Yes, this note is also in Sarnaut, and it's embodied in the people of Kania. In Lightworld, people similar to your race found themselves at the center of events that determine the fate of the entire world. And it's just a forest country unknown to anyone and mostly forgotten. But it lies at the crossroads, and it's the reason the paths of some immortal heroes and the artifacts they kept converged there.
r154412.n: I want to talk about Lightworld

t:
I often say that Chaos beings have infiltrated one of the worlds, and they are waging a war of conquest, but it's not only Chaos that brings destruction. Yes, Chaos is by nature more active, but Darkness also has its supporters.

More often than not, Nihaz's actions turn out to be a temptation, not a threat. While the God of Darkness prefers to act alone, and not through his minions, the Darkness has those who faithfully serve it. Many of those survived the fracture of the previous aeon when the Forgotten One was cast down.

Yes, the ancient god of Darkness left a mark, because the war he once started engulfed the entire universe. I don't know how the henchmen of Darkness made it into Tantibo, but I know there are many of them.

Lurking on the edge of reality, these creatures feed on the fears of mortals. Sparks are also nutritious for them, but they draw their strength from fear. Like the master of Darkness, they never act openly, because in the light they are weak, and in the shadows they are a deadly threat. And what's bad is that the inhabitants of this world are mostly unaware of them. Only a few lucky ones who survived the encounter with Darkness can tell the truth. But they are considered insane in this world.

Who is the true madman - the one who is aware of the danger or the one who doesn't see it, going straight into the trap?
r154413.n: I want to talk about Tantibo

t:
It's strange seeing you among the dead. Among the metal bearers. I'm referring to the Arisen, of course. I took their destiny to the heart when I heard about it. They can't be blamed for taking their own fate. They died prematurely. Their immortality was, in fact, a curse rather than a blessing. Doomed for stagnation, they can't even reproduce. All of it is the consequence of Nihaz's influence, who corrupted Sarn's beautiful creation yet again.

I dug into the memory of the Great Tree and found another good example. Once upon a time there was a race in the world of Trogis. Just like the Arisen, they loved implanting new parts in their bodies.

What can be worse than a sinful synergy of flesh and metal?

When augmenting physical bodies with devices was normalized in the society, this race has become quite aggressive, turning Trogis into a militant world. Its dwellers mastered traveling to other worlds and started spreading their philosophy onto other societies.
r154414.n: I want to ask about Trogis

t:
The precepts of the All-Mother are unknown to this world. There has been a history of transgression of time parallels, wasteful use of elemental energy, and disruption of the balance of life and death, but only one has always lived up to its destiny: the never-ending battle between good and evil. The hero of the world Wuump is outwardly somewhat reminiscent of your Pridens - he always challenged evil in whatever form it manifested itself. I won't list all the dangers he faced. It also happened that one of the Ambrosia crystals, found in the underground network of caves, fell into the hands of an evil that dreamed of changing the world order.

But most of all I was surprised that this world had its own Great Tree, located in the center of the planet. As if an echo of Eden was in the mind of the one who created Wuump. Unfortunately, an evil spirit chose it as its fiefdom, inciting the creatures of this world to various lawless acts.

How this story ended is anyone's guess.

Did heavenly punishment fall on evil, or was the world swallowed up by a dark storm of Nihaz's minions?
r154415.n: I want to talk about Wuump

t:
You are familiar with magic, but there are worlds where instead of full-flowing rivers you can find only drying up streams. The magic in those worlds is the gift of a select few. Such is this world - there is enough progress, but very little magic. But there's a problem: a race of demon-like creatures from the worlds of chaos settled there. Invisible to most, they would freely enter it and commit unthinkable atrocities, if it weren't for the chosen ones who, due to a strange whim of the gods who created that world, turned out to be teenage girls.

It was they who received the magical gift, and it was they who were chosen to fight against the creatures of Chaos hiding in the shadows. No one in that world is aware of the threat that hangs over everyone, no one knows the names of the real defenders of that land.
r154416.n: I want to talk about Yukira

t:
The worlds that lost their patrons or never had them suffer the most. They are under constant threat from technically advanced outer worlds.

All-Mother never supposed that mortals of the outer worlds would be able to travel between them. But Nihaz has altered the Great Circle cycle, enabling many worlds to live beyond their lifespan - and to travel. Sadly, this didn't make their lives any better. Having reached the pinnacle of technical advancements, the worlds commonly fell prey to some disaster. They would either ruin themselves or had to face an external threat.

Yukmid is another world with very little magic. Albeit territorial division, they hardly ever made big wars. Their life would have been nice and easy if only a hostile civilization of aliens hadn't invaded Yukmid.

No one likes uninvited guests, as you understand. Just the same as we weren't happy to welcome you on Eden, dwellers of Yukmid were caught off guard. On top of everything else, the invaders thought it would be a good idea to slave the people of Yukmid. Their cities were under attack. The intruders, much more technically advanced, utterly routed Yukmid's army. It would have become a tragedy but a hero turned up.

You might say that heroes aren't equal to gods. But sometimes a hero can become a god. Are you familiar with the power of faith? What if a world's faith is focused in a single person? Would that change him, and how? All-Mother might have a better explanation. In any case, there was this hero in Yukmid. Everyone in the world could watch him via communication devices. As I said, there's next to no magic in this world but somehow the inhabitants' great faith in a single person imbued him with magical powers. He stopped the invasion army, killed their leaders, and destroyed all of their minions almost single-handedly.  Every victory increased Yukmid people's faith in him, giving him more and more power. He is praised more than anyone in this world.

You are a Sarnaut hero, aren't you? The faith of Sarnaut people could have been the secret of your success.
r154417.n: I want to ask about Yukmid

t:
The universe is a dangerous place even without Nihaz. If it wasn't for monsters, there'd be no heroes... or patrons. The late Eons are dark times we know very little of.

There was a god of Darkness before Nihaz, as the legend would have it. Nobody remembers his name. He had been the adversary of Sarn the Light before All-Mother decided to recreate everything that has ever existed. The truth is that leftovers of the Forgotten army are still roaming in the darkness between worlds.

I came to know that the world of Zynn was building the Gates in order to travel between worlds, just like you did. However, they didn't have a Navigator, like you did. I'm talking about Skulnar. Zynn people had to wander blindly, randomly in the dark.

They managed to open the Gates. As bad luck would have it, madness gushed in. An ancient being from the shards of late Eons' worlds answered their call and sent its armadas through the Gates and into the world of Zynn.

The ancient darkness immediately swallowed the Gates. The ancient being subjugated everyone who was near. Its minions moved forward to take over the world of Zynn.
r154418.n: I want to ask about Zynn

t:
I'll do that!

Good luck, , and be careful.
r154506.n: Right you are. What's one less fruit... Take it.

t: Ugh... alright! I'll help you at least. But you owe me now - don't you forget that.
r154507.n: You'll get another chance. I need to take the fruit back.

t:
Oh yeah?

You know, ... You are a hero. You do important work. And you're on friendly terms with Catherina and Felix.

And me? Just a small research assistant, one of the many cogs in this big machine. You don't even know my name.

I don’t know why you need this nut, but this is my chance to become a bigger cog, which will make me a little happier. Just imagine if they let me do real research! The Expedition would benefit greatly from it. And so would the world...

What do you say, ?
r154508.n: Just give it to me. It's important.

t:
Oh, that's...

That's amazing! I hope I'll be allowed to study them... We must immediately report to the base! I can't wait for show Elena my discovery!

Please don't take it away!
r154509.n: These nuts are the children of sentient aborigines

t: Why would I? I had to risk my neck to get it!

What do you mean, why?

We must study every creature and every plant in this world! Our survival and the success of the entire Expedition depend on it! This won't do any harm to the tree - there is still a bunch of these nuts under it.

Quiet! They'll spot us...

Look what I found! So heavy! I barely managed to bring it here!
r154512.n: Quiet! They'll spot us... Look what I found! So heavy! I barely…

t:
Are you surprised that we also have boys and girls? Such was the will of the All-Mother which made us look like creatures that live on an infinite number of worlds, and which are like you. But the resemblance is only superficial.

We distribute pollen, which then falls on the flowers of the Great Tree, and then fruits form on them. When the time comes, this fruit falls to the ground, and a new Child emerges from it, ready for life in this world and able to speak and walk. I know things are a little different for you, and this is very curious.  Maybe you can tell me about it someday?

My task is to ensure that nothing happens to fallen fruits. Although they are well protected by their dense skin, anything can happen, and it would be a tragedy to lose a new member of the tribe. After all, they might be the one destined to become the germ of a new Great Tree!

Look at me. At any of us. You see the fruit on our heads? This fruit is the focus of our life force. The fruit is the germ of a future Great Tree. This is the true purpose of our existence - to keep the cycle going.

Sooner or later our Tree will die. But new shoots will sprout from its remains, spawned by one of us. Isn't this a true miracle?
r154530.n: Hello, what do you do here?

t: I'm getting more and more convinced that we should stay away from the gods. Do we really want to drag that lady to Sarnaut to straighten things up by her own rules? I don't think that anyone's going to be happy about it. On the other hand, it might be not as bad as we think. She could have thrown the trial to impress her own followers. Let's see how she will act.
r154538.n: What do you think about the trial?

t: You wear a hard shell, but your bark underneath is quite soft.  We are stronger than you on the inside.
r154543.n: You wear a hard shell, but your bark underneath is quite soft. We are…

t:
What do we do in the current situation? A long-range recon, of course. We need to know what forces the locals have, where they main cities lie. We'll know then where to strike. To do it, we need a small group. Three people, five tops. You can make a great leader for the recon party.

If we don't do it, we risk losing the initiative. The animals' attacks get more and more massive and powerful. They're wary about approaching the base, but it's only a matter of time. Although they use primitive weapons, their power is in numbers.

Here's my solution: either they stop attacking us or we'll kick them back into the swamp they crawled out of.

Welcome to Eden. You're outside Sarnaut. Keep that in mind while you're here. This world is dangerous. Every creature outside this base is dangerous, be it an animal, a bird, or a plant. The local population is also extremely aggressive. They hated us at the first sight... and we hated them. Beware of the savages with arrows. We don't have the Purgatory here, there's no Servant of Tensess to resurrect you. If you're dead, you're dead. No matter how much I want everyone to return home safely, I know that many will have to stay here for the eternity.

That's what I'm talking about...

These gods are useless. They are nothing but trouble.

I'm tired of this. We'll solve our problems ourselves. If we can get enough Ambrosia, then we'll be as powerful as the gods.

From now on, anyone who stands in our way will be crushed. If the Children try to stop us, we will burn everything to the ground!

Now report back to Catherina about everything you've learned. I'm preparing a general offensive to protect our Harvesters.
r154587.n: Well... it's not going as well as we hoped.

t: Yes? Or maybe you got them to agree to help us in our fight against Nihaz? Is this All-Mother ready to join us?
Haven't we given you enough time? What have you been up to? Your task was to arrange for us to be allowed to harvest Ambrosia. What have you accomplished?
r154589.n: Why did you decide to break the truce?

t:
I don't know whose side you're on!

Go back to your tribe! Get out of my sight!

How foul...

We agreed that the harvesting of Ambrosia would be stopped! But your mechanoids started harvesting it in the Ambrosia Valley, a sacred place at the very roots of the Great Tree...

We are not going to tolerate this kind of insolence any longer. Our warriors are going into battle to throw you out of this world!
r154592.n: Je ne sais pas de quoi vous parlez !

t: Then go to the Expedition's camp and deliver my message! Your tribesmen will answer for this betrayal!
r154593.n: I had nothing to do with this!

t:
Your tribesmen cannot be trusted!

We agreed that the harvesting of Ambrosia would be stopped! But your mechanoids started harvesting it in the Ambrosia Valley, the sacred place at the very roots of the Great Tree...

We are not going to tolerate this kind of insolence any longer. Our warriors are going into battle to throw you out of this world!
r154594.n: You are crazy! I'm on your side!

t: Return to your tribesmen, you vile traitor! Get out of my sight!

Foul hypocrite! All this time, you and the others have been working for the Expedition!

We agreed that the harvesting of Ambrosia would be stopped! But your mechanoids started harvesting it in the Ambrosia Valley, the sacred place at the very roots of the Great Tree...

We are not going to tolerate this kind of insolence any longer. Our warriors are going into battle to throw you out of this world!
r154596.n: What gives you the right to say that?

t: Traitor! You are all traitors! How treacherous! How deceitful!

Perhaps you've had enough of the gods? It's time to take fate into your own hands.

Do you want to fight Nihaz?

But do you really need to call on some goddess to help you? What do you personally think about it?

You have to decide.
r154653.n: What do you suggest I do?

t:
I saw your Catherina study the ruins of an "unknown ancient civilization"... What do you think happened to this ruined city?

Once upon a time there were travelers just like you. They built houses, looked for metals in the ground, cut down trees...

The All-Mother destroyed them all. No other alternative is acceptable to her. The same fate awaits you, if you listen blindly to her. Think about it.

Don't want to be strung along anymore?

This ideal little world is not that simple at all... There was a lot going on here you weren't told about.
r154655.n: What do you want to tell me about Eden?

t: I opened their eyes, exposing the blatant injustice of what happened to them.
I extended their lives as best I could. But she? She could give them new ones. But she won't do that.
Cruel, senseless sentence - just like everything my mother does!
They used to be the same as your new friends, but their Tree's lifespan has come to an end. Now they are doomed.
Do you still not understand why they don't want to die?
r154660.n: What are you trying to say?

t:
So far, all out attempts to communicate with the locals were futile. We tried, we really tried talking, we even tried to trade. They simply hate the guts of our campaign. Did Klavdia expect us to find allies here? She was wrong.

Not to mention the mysterious goddess we're looking for. At this point, I think it's just a myth. We haven't come across a single god here. Just the mad beasts, mad plants, and mad locals...

You might get through to them. I'd hate for another war to begin. It's crazy expensive. Our main focus is on gathering ambrosia and sending it back to Sarnaut. You'll have to walk the extra mile... and every mile in between.

We're here for ambrosia. The price for ambrosia is over ten thousand crystals per pound. It pays for the whole Expedition, which is quite expensive, I must say. It pays both for Catherina's research and for the search of... whoever we're looking for. Some goddess or something. The local savages are putting the entire operation at risk. As if mad beasts and plants weren't enough! I want you to help us work out a diplomatic solution and avoid war.

r154998.n: I read you loud and clear!

t: Come in! Do you copy? As you can see, this is a multipurpose device for long distance communication.
r154999.n: Come in! Do you copy? As you can see, this is a multipurpose device…

t:
Yes. There's something. But it's too early to draw conclusions...

Although... What other options are there? In short, I discovered some ruins. It's a whole city, but it's overgrown. It might be thousands of years old - all the metal has long turned to dust. Only the foundations and parts of the walls remain.

I guess your friends had nothing to do with it. I doubt they'd build with stone, which means... there was another civilization here. I need to find out what happened to it.

Here I'm going to say my goodbyes and this: you don't have much time - Felix and Ivan are chomping at the bit, they need the Ambrosia, and your Children won't let our harvesters into the forest. They want you to talk to the All-Mother about harvesting it.

That's all. Goodbye.
r155001.n: Ask if she has found anything interesting.

t:
How is it going? How is it going?! Are you serious?!

I'm sitting at this wrecked base in the forest, trying to figure out what's going on. No apprentices, no amenities, nothing! Even the toilet is not working here, let alone scientific equipment. I'll have to wait for Felix and Ivan to send me replacement parts.

And there are no signs of Herbert and Elena. It's like they vanished into thin air. If they are not with the All-Mother, then I don’t know what to think. Herbert doesn't seem like someone who'd get killed by a wandering stump. And Elena is smarter than she looks.

Oh yeah?

Perhaps we could use this... If Nihaz is a problem for the All-Mother, she might help Sarnaut - the enemy of my enemy is my friend, right?

Try to explain to her that we're on the same side. Yes, we harvest the Ambrosia, but only because we desperately need it, and if those rotten things are a threat to her, we could help her fight them. We have quite an arsenal here, after all.
Come in! Do you copy? I repeat. Do you copy? Can you hear me? Tep take this rusty thing! Do you copy? Come in!
r155004.n: Come in! Do you copy? I repeat. Do you copy? Can you hear me? Tep take…

t: Stay away from my plans. Ciao!

r155020.n: Gather your people. I'll take you to the base.

t: Catherina closed the world but it never stopped you. You found a way in.
r155021.n: Catherina closed the world but it never stopped you. You found a way in.

t: This is one of the Expedition's harvesters. Have they gone this far?
r155191.n: This is one of the Expedition's harvesters. Have they gone this far?

t: Uh, that's much better. Thanks. I'll find my own way from here when it gets quiet.
You're here! How fortunate. First, the aborigines attacked, then the machines went mad, so I just ran... and ran, and ran. And then I found myself here. I'm stuck. Will you help me free?
r155275.n: You're here! How fortunate. First, the aborigines attacked, then the…

t: I'm waiting for the right moment. Don't worry, I'll get the others. I'd rather land in woodfaces' prison than in the middle of the rise of the machines.
r155276.n: I'm waiting for the right moment. Don't worry, I'll get the others.…

t: I've lost my goggles! Can you believe it? They should be here but I can't find them, I'm almost blind! Will you help?
That's a thing to thank for! I should go to prison, you say? Oh, well then... I'm sure you'll think of something to let us out. I'll take a short breather and go.
Ugh, where are they? I can't go anywhere without my goggles.
r155282.n: Ugh, where are they? I can't go anywhere without my goggles.

t: Yes, yes. The prison. I remember. I'll be on my way soon. I don't want to rush to get to prison.
r155283.n: Yes, yes. The prison. I remember. I'll be on my way soon. I don't want…

t: I know! You're the messenger of the green people! Do they want me back in their prison? Alright. I know, they rule everything and everyone here.
r155286.n: I know! You're the messenger of the green people! Do they want me back…

t: And those who fail to obey them will suffer... the consequences. Why would they need our cows, though?
r155287.n: And those who fail to obey them will suffer... the consequences. Why…

r155290.n: I'll be on my way then?

t: And then you go on breaking the remaining mechanoids, and I'll go to prison. We must go apart, because you attract too much attention. I'll sneak quietly in the shadow. I'll see you there. And then we'll figure out what to do with the prisoners. Alright, chop-chop.

...that they're easy to persuade to let us go. As... as goodwill ambassadors!

Honestly, I hate the whole idea of the stand between the Expedition and the Forestfolk. We're nothing but occupants on this land. We broke in, started tearing down the trees, pumping out ambrosia... I know it's for a good cause, but I deeply hate the approach.

You see, the green people are pacifists by nature, right? Aha. So they sent you to break down mechanoids. They don't want to do it with their own hands. That's also the reason why we all ended up in prison and not dead.

So, they're pacifists. This means...
Do you think I'm a woman in need? Haven't you learned anything from Ferris? No way. I escaped to think through a rescue plan. And here's what I'm thinking...
r155294.n: Do you think I'm a woman in need? Haven't you learned anything from…

t:
Yes, our research.

The results are very curious.

As I said, the builders of this city were quite advanced. They mined metals, dug quarries.

The settlement was destroyed by someone else. It looks like an external attack. There are traces of strikes and repairs. It stopped helping at some point, though. They either left the city or all died.

I'll try to find out more. Return to All-Mother and try to make that deal.

How curious. Another Nihaz's child? The goddess of Darkness and Death?

She's a very dangerous creature, threatening both us and All-Mother. We must convince the willful goddess to unite our forces against Nihaz's messengers.

I also wonder whom Hirkalla was talking about. What are the Sparks that came from Sarnaut to Eden? If the Sage is the Umoir god that, as you say, has left our world... then who is the Madman?

A Great Mage that we know nothing about? A new ancient god? If Klavdia didn't have Tep's Spark, I could think that it was him. But she's had it since the Pyramid.

Gah!

Don't get me wrong, I'm happy that we've found them. I hope they'll get in touch soon. But the Children... they won't let us to a thing on Eden. What are we going to do? We'll have to make a deal and exchange ambrosia for something. I wonder what they'd be interested in...

As to mechanoids, they're in defense state. They attack everything that seems hostile... which is pretty much everything around here. I must say, Ivan and Felix were outraged. You broke down a lot of very expensive machines. I'll try and justify your actions for them.
r155301.n: Report what happened to the Expedition, Herbert, and Elena

t: Ask me. Child of Sarn. But be quick, the beast won't wait forever.

We need to survive the fight. The Treebor is merciless - if you fall, it will trample you.

Mint can protect you. If you fall, give her a sign, and the forest charms will protect you.

When the Treebor is weakened, we need to wait until it gets distracted and drops its guard. Then we can finish it off. At the right moment, give the command to Clover. His final blow will be precise and merciful, sending the beast to the beginning of the cycle.

Is your heart ready?
r155343.n: I'll collect the sap - then what?

t:
Rage will make its strength fill its veins. Each drop of its sap that falls on the ground is priceless - collect them.

But even in rage, there should be balance, otherwise the sap of the beast will be filled not with strength, but with madness. Don't let the rage of the Treebor dissipate, but don't let it go berserk either.
r155344.n: So we'll make it angry - then what?

t:
You will be attacking it.

Give me a sign, and I'll poke it with my thorn. Its skin is thick, but the sap on the tip of my thorn will keep making it angrier.
r155345.n: So how are we doing this?

t: We're tired of waiting. I'll tell you everything, just be willing to listen...
r155438.n: Ask Felix why the truce was broken

t:
Making demands? I must have misheard.

What right do you have to demand anything from me? Perhaps you've become too attached to these aborigines? Do you want to be executed for treason?

Your task was to arrange for us to be allowed to harvest Ambrosia. What have you accomplished?
r155439.n: I demand that you take the Harvesters back to the base!

t:
I'm tired of waiting. We're wasting time. How much longer do we have to wait for something to change?

These negotiations are a joke.

Your task was to arrange for us to be allowed to harvest Ambrosia. What have you accomplished?

At my request, they arrived at the agreed meeting place. I guess they would like to talk to you.

It is your example that can inspire other tribes as much as it did us.

Try to convince them.
r155461.n: How do I speak with them?

t:
Yes, that's right.

The tribes Evergreen, Deciduous, and Blooming. Their Great Trees are located to the west, north, and east of our Valley. News of what is happening here has already reached them. However, it won't be easy to persuade them to join us.
r155462.n: Rhubarb told me you called the tribal leaders

t:
No, our warriors haven't finished training the other tribes yet.

If you can help us defend the Valley, more warriors can go on this mission. Complete the tasks of Camellia, Sumac, and Elm. By doing this, you will significantly speed up the training of our army.

Good news! We have every chance to drive the Expedition out of the Valley.

We are preparing for the final attack, but apparently our enemies are doing the same. The decisive battle is about to begin, and we must be ready.
r155468.n: The tribes will answer our call!

t: The All-Mother's power is the power of life itself. Life offers countless opportunities...
r155469.n: The All-Mother's power is the power of life itself. Life offers…

t: We are the children of progress People once fought with sticks and stones, now we have weapons that can affect even gods.
r155479.n: We are the children of progress People once fought with sticks and…

t:
I don't think, I act! Let's blow something up, okay?

So many new impressions! So many new ideas! It's time to do something! My hands are itching! I need to create! Ooooh, just give me a workshop and a heap of nuts and bolts! I know I can come up with something! Just look at all the saws lying around! Imagination running wild!

Come on, go and find Catherina! Tell her I'm ready for action!
r155568.n: What do you think about the new world?

t:
In short, we need this crystalline concentrate... But this is not Suslanger, there are no crystals here. So we need to distill liquid Ambrosia into crystalline form - and this requires time and a lot of this liquid Ambrosia.

And that's another problem. Those Children are vicious. They don't let us collect the Ambrosia. They're hitting us on all fronts, yeah.

If you want Ambrosia to flow through the pipeline, then you must inspire the soldiers with your own example. How?

Complete a few of my tasks, and we'll win, you'll see. As soon as everything is ready, come see me.

By the way, lest you think I'm sitting around twiddling my thumbs here - you'll be able to see the progress yourself. The more you do, the sooner it will be finished.

Hello there, chief! I've always wanted to blow everything up, yeah. You and Catherina have interesting ideas! I love it!

Well, I'll do it. I'll build you a mana bomb in a couple of days, if need be...

But the Ambrosia part - now there's a problem.
r155570.n: Ask about creating an Ambrosia mana bomb

t: Come on, chief, I need more Ambrosia. I'm telling you - if you want Ambrosia to flow through the pipeline, then you need to inspire the soldiers with your own example. Complete my tasks, and we'll win.

The component was taken by this elf, Herbert. Maybe he needed it for something, or maybe he is some kind of saboteur, yeah. Ask him to return it.

Without this part, no big boom is gonna happen.

Yes, chief. Almost everything is ready, but... one component is missing. Yes, that always seems to be the case.

True, but this time I know who has it. After all, we have cameras all over the place, so no one can get through undetected.

If they had worked at Gates-3, then no Alice would have been able to steal the Chronophone, and you wouldn't have had to wallow in the desert.
Great, chief! This is exactly what we need! It’s good that you did it quickly, because I’m being rushed here, too.
Woah, look at all these new constructions! I wonder where they found the time for it.
r155580.n: Woah, look at all these new constructions! I wonder where they found…

t:
Actually she didn't even care about us - she was laser-focused on you. So when the panic among my colleagues subsided, Elena and I were able to get everyone to the Gates base.

We're helping Catherina with her research of Eden.
r155582.n: How did you manage to escape after meeting Hirkalla?

t:
What will be the cost of this victory? If we do this, are we any better than Nihaz? He also destroys worlds for the purposes we don't even understand...

Well, if that's your decision, then so be it. But I want no part of this. I have a proposition - you will let us leave Eden, and I will give you the component. Everything that happens after that will be on your conscience.

Yes, I know Felix implemented high-security protocols, but Elena seems to have an idea. Speak with her.

Hmm, indeed...

Well, since you're here, let's talk about it.

Felix is a madman, a military sociopath willing to burn everything down. But you… I honestly thought you were different.

What you are about to do... it's a crime, pure and simple!
r155585.n: Nogrom Junior says you have some important component

t: Here. And be far away when it does its thing. And now goodbye. Soon Elena and I will leave Eden.

Murk is an old friend. He is true to himself, and I respect that. As for you...

I hope we will all meet again under much better circumstances. Once again, I don't approve of your plan - though perhaps we shouldn't have come to Eden at all...
Yes, I did not expect this when I agreed to visit this world.
r155589.n: Yes, I did not expect this when I agreed to visit this world.

t: Not bad, though we really didn't expect to go to war when we mounted a scientific expedition. If I'd known, I would've brought a few extra things with me.

We need one of those codes that are changed daily to activate the Gates... One that would get us onto the Star Trail.

Of course, no one will give it to you, but it looks like our crafty and cunning Priden managed to get the password. I'd ask him myself, but it would be too suspicious. But no one would suspect you.
r155593.n: What can I do to help?

t:
Ah, Herbert made up his mind after all. I also think we're done here. The natives are extremely hostile, and Felix with his soldiery is not the company I want to keep.

We could visit one of the other worlds on the Star Trail... It would be so romantic!
I always felt like our adventures would eventually take us to a place we wouldn't be able to get out of.
r155595.n: I always felt like our adventures would eventually take us to a place…

t:
Well, that suits me just fine.

Actually, it's what we initially wanted.

I just need to be sure that she won't try to impose her rules on anyone when she comes into our world. Otherwise, I'm not ready to give up technology at the behest of some goddess, even if she wants the best for everyone.

"Has a shard of Sarn in her" - what is she trying to say? What?!

quests: We are all part of the cycle of life

r155648.n: Yes, if you stop this war

t:
Dear child, if I imposed my vision on all the worlds, would we have the diversity Verbena must have told you about? When mortals choose their path, I do not interfere...

I have no power to destroy what is created. I am a creator, not a destroyer.

Your immortality primarily harms you. I could heal you... but you don't want that. So be it.
Your destructive tendencies scare me. Is this the foundation Sarn laid when he created you?
r155656.n: Your destructive tendencies scare me. Is this the foundation Sarn laid…

t:
The respect of the entire Sarnaut!

And generous rewards in Dendrite Coins. Our guys will restock your ammunition for them, and they might even procure some rare equipment.

The better you perform in battle, the more you get.

Fight for the Sources, destroy the enemies, deliver the Seeds to our Invaders, and eliminate the Healers. Every action counts. I personally oversee everything.

All clear?

Go!
r155733.n: The respect of the entire Sarnaut! And generous rewards in Dendrite…

t:
These are rare and powerful sorceresses of Eden. They are trying to heal Cypress and ruin our plans.

I order you to take them out first.

Healers also consume Seeds of Power to become stronger or respawn. Keep the enemy from capturing the Sources and eliminate those who carry the Seeds.

That way we won't let the enemy win.
r155734.n: These are rare and powerful sorceresses of Eden. They are trying to…

t:
They are our key to victory. Only their fire can burn through Cypress's strong bark.

But there is a drawback: these machines target only the Treant. They need your protection. Keep the local savages away from them.

If they break an Invader, only a new Seed of Power can repair it.

While the Invader is alive, use the Seeds to increase its combat power and destroy the Cypress even faster.

This will give us an advantage over the Healers.
r155735.n: They are our key to victory. Only their fire can burn through…

t:
A Seed of Power is a powerful concentrate of local energy. Without this power, we won't be able to bring down Cypress.

Captured Sources produce Seeds. They are small at first, but they ripen over a couple of minutes.

The ripe seed must be taken from the Source and quickly delivered to the center of the valley, so we can install and fuel our A-22 Invaders.
r155736.n: A Seed of Power is a powerful concentrate of local energy. Without…

t:
There are four Sources of power in the valley. If we capture them, we can get fuel for the Invaders.

But the enemy is vigilant. If the Children control the Source, you will have to chop all the Source Protectors for firewood first, otherwise you won't be able to access its power.

Then enter the Source and concentrate. If no one interrupts you, the Source will obey and start producing Seeds of Power for us.
r155737.n: There are four Sources of power in the valley. If we capture them, we…

t:
Listen to me carefully, fighter!

In the center of the valley is the largest deposit of the Ambrosia. It is guarded by this giant log, Cypress. It hates us.

Now it's weak. Our mission is to bring it down. If the Cypress falls, we will win and take control of the valley.

The natives will try to stop us and heal the Treant. If they succeed, we will have to retreat and leave the valley.

Cypress has strong bark. Our A-22 Invaders can penetrate it, but they need powerful fuel from the local Sources.

Listen up!

It's too early for you to fight, soldier! First deal with Comrade Catherina's tasks and decide which side you are on.

But I respect curiosity. Need a briefing?
r155740.n: It's too early for you to fight, soldier! First deal with Comrade…

t:
Science division, as you know, is headed by Catherina.

She didn't like the idea at first, but I managed to persuade her. Now your task is to help her create this device.

And my task will be to deliver it to the enemy.
r155742.n: Find out what needs to be done to create an Ambrosia mana bomb.

t:
I've been thinking about how we can win this, and I may have a solution.

Our resources are incomparable with what the natives have. However, we have a serious advantage - our determination and willingness to make any sacrifices.

We also have our technology.

Imperial engineers once created a unique weapon - a mana bomb. It's good but not powerful enough to secure us a victory.

But the Ambrosia... its power is unimaginable. We can combine our technologies and the resources of this world, and then no one will stand in our way.

Yasker is too weak to fight the Goddess of Darkness. But Catherina and I are going to challenge her!

As for the war here in Eden... It doesn't change anything!

On the contrary, our task has become even more important. To gather strength to fight this… Hirkalla, we need even more Ambrosia! And even if I stay here alone, I will continue to harvest it!

I hope you're still on our side.
We will take what we need. We will capture the valley - and the power of the Ambrosia will be our weapon against Nihaz.
r155745.n: We will take what we need. We will capture the valley - and the power…

t:
A reward? We are protecting our home!

I know. Eden is not your home, Child of Sarn. You stand against your people to help us.

Fight for us, and I will generously bestow on you the Tears of the All-Mother You can pay our craftsmen with them for the supplies you need.

 The better you perform in battle, the greater reward I can promise you.

Fight for the Sources, eliminate the enemies, deliver the Seeds to our Healers, and destroy the Invaders. All-Mother sees everything. Each feat will be counted.
r155763.n: What will I get for participating in the battle?

t:
These iron monsters, created by the children of Sarn, are able to burn through Cypress's bark with their fire.

The expedition captures the Sources and uses the energy of the Seeds of Power to create and strengthen these monsters.

Destroy the Invaders as soon as they appear, and do not allow the enemy to use the Sources and Seeds of Power for their own purposes!

Only the great daughters of Eden can heal the wounds of Cypress.

But they have to focus entirely on healing, so they can't defend themselves. Protect them from the enemy.

If a Healer falls, only a new Seed can bring her back to life.

If you offer the Seed to a living Healer, her strength will increase for a while, and Cypress's wounds will heal even faster.

This is how we will help Cypress survive against the Invaders.

The seed of power is a powerful concentration of the energy of life itself. Without them, we can't protect Cypress.

Seeds are born in the Sources and belong to those who own the Source. They are small at first but ripen quickly.

Take the ripe seed from the source and deliver it to the heart of the valley as quickly as possible to revive our great Healers or strengthen those who are fighting for the life of the Cypress.

The valley is nourished by four Sources of power, and by nature they are free. But we can turn the power of the Source to our advantage.

First, if the source is already captured by the Expedition, you will have to defeat all the Source Protectors first, otherwise you won't be able to access its power.

Then enter the Source and concentrate. If no one interrupts your concentration, the Source will begin to produce Seeds of Power for us.

Look - all the rivers of the Ambrosia flow to the center of the valley. The mighty Cypress guards the Ambrosia there.

Now it's weak. Several times a day, the enemy attacks him, trying to break him. If Cypress falls, the Expedition will win and take control of the valley.

If we manage to fully heal Cypress, he will put the enemy to flight, and the valley will remain ours.

Our great Healers can heal the Cypress, but they need nourishment from the Seeds of Power. You can get them from the Sources along the edges of the valley.

But first things first.
r155769.n: Look - all the rivers of the Ambrosia flow to the center of the…

t:
You are eager to go into battle, but can we trust you, Child of Sarn? First learn the lessons of the All-Mother and decide which side you are on.

But if you want, I'll tell you about our war. Perhaps this will influence your choice.

Are you listening carefully?

quests: Battle for Ambrosia: Capturing the Sources

r155770.n: You are eager to go into battle, but can we trust you, Child of Sarn?…

t:
Waterlily has already volunteered to help spread the word to our closest neighbors.

I believe their representatives will arrive here soon. You'll need to talk to Waterlily and then get the other tribal leaders to join us in our fight against the Expedition.
r155772.n: Find out what needs to be done to form an alliance

t:
When the Expedition arrived at Eden, we began to change. The Children who were once hunters have become warriors, our animals have grown powerful fangs, and our flowers have sprouted thorns.

Other tribes are still peaceful. Living far from the Valley, they do not know troubles and sorrows. They did not deal with the deadly machines and the reanimated bodies of the Old Tribe.

So enlisting their help is not enough. You need to train them.

quests: Battle for Ambrosia: Capturing the Sources

t:
Unthinkable! Without the All-Mother our worlds will be swallowed by darkness! We need to find a way to tell the other gods what happened...

As for the war with the Expedition... What happened doesn't change anything!

On the contrary, our task has become even more important. To gather strength to fight this… Hirkalla, we need to protect Eden! And even if I stay here alone, I will continue to defend it!

I hope you're still on our side.

quests: Battle for Ambrosia: Capturing the Sources

t: The Great Tree gave us life. Now it's our turn to protect it.

quests: Battle for Ambrosia: Capturing the Sources

r155775.n: The Great Tree gave us life. Now it's our turn to protect it.

t: The Children of Sarn came to our world in an hour of great need.
r155780.n: The Children of Sarn came to our world in an hour of great need.

t:
So the time has come. We'll go to our tribes and summon those who have arrived!

The invaders believed that this land will submit to them, but we will that we can protect our world!

Report our decision to Waterlily.
r155783.n: We are ready to set out!

t:
Yes, we will answer your call!

We will bring not just the warriors of our tribes, but also members of those who live in other parts of our world. Everything is in motion, stories and songs about what is happening here are shared throughout Eden, and the Children are ready to throw the invaders out of this world!

Although there are many strange machines on their side, Eden itself is on ours. The Children are fearless and not afraid of death.
r155784.n: Are you willing to aid us?

t: The All-Mother sees everything. She warned us that you would come.
r155785.n: The All-Mother sees everything. She warned us that you would come.

t:
We organize trainings. The warriors of your tribe will train the warriors of our tribes.

Alas, if they come to us, your lands will be left without defenders. If you can replace them for a while, then we can finish this training sooner.

To do this, complete the tasks given to you by Camelia, Sumac, and Elm.

quests: Making Friends with Grass and Trees

t:
Waterlily has already told us about your troubles, although only rumors have reached us until now.

Yes, this Expedition, which comes from the same world as you, poses a considerable danger.

I agree that we should all work together. The tribes of Eden will unite to fight the outlanders.

However, you must understand that we don't have warriors, only hunters.
Outlander! There hasn't been anyone like you in Eden for thousands of years!
r155799.n: Outlander! There hasn't been anyone like you in Eden for thousands of…

t: Creatures like you keep trying to kill us. I will fight to protect the Children of the All-Mother!
r155802.n: Creatures like you keep trying to kill us. I will fight to protect the…

t: So it was you who took down Waterlily and Reed? If It had been me...
r155806.n: So it was you who took down Waterlily and Reed? If It had been me...

t: Not that much of justice, to be honest. Ugh, them gods... all they can is make up tangled rules and punish sinners. Is it our fault that there's immortality in Sarnaut? Have we been asking for it? They forced me to drink dragon's blood, did you know that? Whatev. They're the bosses, like the Kanians say, hah. Let's try to figure out whether they can help us.
r155810.n: What do you think about the trial?

t:
Me? Well, it wasn't Catherina who sent us to this world, but Klavdia, so I will try to do what she asked us to do. Try to persuade the mother to help against Nihaz, that is.

And what the Expedition is doing there doesn't really matter to me. Life, you know, taught me to stay away from all these Xadaganian mechanical things. I think you understand me.

The most important question is what you're planning to do, heh.
r155811.n: What are you planning to do?

t:
Sort of. The scouts report that the Mechanoids are heading for the Valley.

Which means there will be another fight here soon, nuts and bolts flying every which way.

However, if Felix thinks everything will be simple, he'll be disappointed. The Children are also decent warriors, and they are getting stronger every day.
r155812.n: Is the Expedition planning an offensive?

t:
In a situation like this, I'm on my side first and foremost, heh. I'd rather keep my head.

But look, Klavdia sent us here, right? She knew Catherina and Felix would start something, so she told us to find the All-Mother and ask for help. The war with the Children will not help our mission in any way - rather the opposite, heh.

 In short, our goal is to save Sarnaut, not the Expedition.  You do as you wish, and I will stay here.
r155813.n: Will you side with the Children?

t:
Yep. They didn't want to wait until we're finished here. Though I doubt they actually expected us to do anything. We were probably sent here like lambs to be slaughtered, with the expectation that the All-Mother would condemn us and this would be his... what was it... casus belli, yes.

But this Xadaganian is fooling himself if he thinks this fight will be a cakewalk. The Children are already good warriors, they trained while we were just sitting here.
r155814.n: Felix and Ivan decided not to wait after all.

t:
You think so? But I'm not sure. Look, Klavdia sent us here, right? What did she tell us?

Help Catherina and Co.? Or make arrangements with the All-Mother?

The latter. And if we start fighting with the Children now, what will happen? Will we reach agreement? Or we'll get beans? And what about Nihaz, then? He'll just come and destroy everything?

In short, you do as you wish, but I prefer to stay away from this Felix. I'll sit here, heh.
r155815.n: We need to help the Expedition!

t:
Yeah, sort of. The peacekeeping mission turned into simple recon, heh. The Committee loved doing that back in the day. Well, we've seen a lot...

But I'll tell you what - this battle won't be easy. There are considerable forces on the side of the Children, and they are, in fact, not bad warriors. If Felix sticks his head in here, there will be losses.
Here is the thing. Catherina sent a message telling everyone to come back. I think you understand what that means.

The most important advice is to survive. So don't go asking for trouble. Although... We'll probably end up in deep sh... Well, you know.

If we survive, I'm going to head home. Why? So many orcs unsupervised - who knows what they'll cook up this time. So no more adventures, I'm going to stay home.
r155818.n: Do you have any advice for me?

t:
Well, we really stepped into it. And everything was going so well: there's a truce between the Empire and the League, and we're fighting Nihaz together...

But no, even if we win now, things won't be the same.

War will probably break out again, perhaps between other groups. Like the Orcs and Gibberlings against Zem and Elves, heh.
r155819.n: What do you think about the situation?

t: Whew, I thought we were dead, hah.
r155820.n: Whew, I thought we were dead, hah.

t: Well? I'm losing my mind here.
r155822.n: Well? I'm losing my mind here.

t: Wow, looks like we're in a bind.
r155823.n: Wow, looks like we're in a bind.

t:
Obviously, we must help the Children defend their world. I think it would be right.

But if you want to help the Expedition, I won't judge you for that choice. Though I'll be sorry if our ways part.

I don't think the All-Mother is right about everything, but I'm not sure Catherina and Felix should be followed either.

That's right. The Children or the Expedition.

On the one hand, representatives of our home world who came here for the Ambrosia. A power that has the potential to make us gods.

And then there are the Children, the inhabitants of this world who shouldn't have to suffer because we need this resource. And a powerful goddess who seems to be able to help us.

The choice is not easy.

What do I do? I know better than anyone in Sarnaut what it's like to follow the path that Nihaz mapped out for you. And you know, I don't think that's right at all.

It's great to be powerful - but at what cost? Elleken committed unthinkable atrocities for his own purposes. Tep doomed his people. Ath-Zak was a hero who rejected the temptations of Nihaz. So what do I want to be? A hero or a villain?
r155830.n: We'll have to pick a side.

t:
I'm glad you agree with me. So we'll be on the same side. Sarnaut's interests are not focused on ravaging other worlds. Verbena told me that Nihaz had plundered many worlds, stealing their power. We must choose another way.

We will help the Children defend their home and drive back the invaders who do not represent all of Sarnaut.
r155831.n: I think you are making the right choice!

t:
Yes, I noticed that you are learning the lessons of the All-Mother. And Skulnar is also leaning towards the Children. But what should I do? You see, my father would of course have chosen to side with the Expedition, but right now I'm not so sure that I want to be on the same side.

I know better than anyone in Sarnaut what it's like to follow the path that Nihaz mapped out for you. And you know, I don't think that's right at all.

It's great to be powerful - but at what cost? Elleken committed unthinkable atrocities for his own purposes. Tep doomed his people. Ath-Zak was a hero who rejected the temptations of Nihaz. So what do I want to be? A hero or a villain?

It's a pity you don't agree with me. So we'll be fighting on different sides. But Sarnaut's interests are not focused on ravaging other worlds. Verbena told me that Nihaz had plundered many worlds, stealing their power. We must choose another way.

Yes, the members of the Expedition are our compatriots. Not all of them, though. I think it's more important to protect this world which could be our ally!

Yes, I saw you running errands for them. But it looks like Skulnar is leaning towards the Children. But what should I do? You see, my father would of course have chosen to side with the Expedition, but right now I'm not so sure that I want to be on the same side.

I know better than anyone in Sarnaut what it's like to follow the path that Nihaz mapped out for you. And you know, I don't think that's right at all.

It's great to be powerful - but at what cost? Elleken committed unthinkable atrocities for his own purposes. Tep doomed his people. Ath-Zak was a hero who rejected the temptations of Nihaz. So what do I want to be? A hero or a villain?
Apparently our friends at the camp did not wait for the end of your training. Now we have to decide what we're going to do.

I don't really understand the Children's plan yet. We have no commanders, and it looks like the plan is to rely on numbers to overwhelm the enemy. But the base is well-defended and it won't be easy to break through the perimeter, as you've seen earlier.

We can only hope - and I think the scouts confirm this - that our enemies will be even more stupid and will attack first.
r155836.n: Do you have any advice for me?

t:
I think that... when this operation was initially planned, a mistake was made. We thought Catherina had become wiser, but she is still the same as she was when she started that madness on Umoir. But Klavdia made the biggest mistake. We consider her almost infallible but as it turns out, she can't be trusted either.

The only one who is able to think sensibly in this situation is Zayan.

My father was wary of him for a reason. Even with all his experience and power, Elleken is in many ways inferior to the great Historian.
r155837.n: What do you think about the situation?

t: I admit, you've been lucky in trials lately.
r155838.n: I admit, you've been lucky in trials lately.

t: It's pretty nice around here. I like it.
r155839.n: It's pretty nice around here. I like it.

t:
